title: Simultaneous generic freeness of annihilator and principal quotients
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative integral domain, $K=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$ its localization at the zero prime [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], and $B$ a commutative finite type $A$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Let $b\in B$ have nonzero image $b\otimes1$ in $B\otimes_AK$ [def-weil-module-base-change]. Define $I=\operatorname{Ann}_B(b)=\{x\in B:bx=0\}$, $C=B/I$, and $D=B/bB$, where $bB=\{bx:x\in B\}$. Both $C$ and $D$ are finite type $A$-algebras, and $0	o C\xrightarrow{\iota}B	o D	o0$ is an exact sequence of $A$-modules, with $\iota( ar x)=bx$ and the last map the quotient. For every $0

Here subscripts denote ring or module localization [def-weil-ring-localization-away, def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away]. The localized sequence $0	o C_g\xrightarrow{\iota_g}B_g	o D_g	o0$ is exact, $C_g

proof.text: The images in $C$ and $D$ of a finite algebra generating family of $B$ still generate: a polynomial expression in $B$ maps to the same expression in either quotient [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Both quotients are therefore finite type. The map $\iota(x+I)=bx$ is well-defined since $bI=0$, is $A$-linear, and has zero kernel since $bx=0$ means $x\in I$. Its image is exactly $bB$, which is the kernel of the surjection $B\to D$. This proves the asserted unlocalized short exact sequence.

source.place: Tag 0575, lemma-nonreduced-in-neighbourhood, annihilator quotient and multiplication sequence; explicit fraction calculations

proof.text: For $0\ne a\in A$, suppose $C_a=0$. Then $1_C/1=0$, so the fraction criterion of [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away] gives $a^r1_C=0$ for some $r\geq0$. Thus the image of $a^r$ in $B$ lies in $I$, giving $a^rb=0$. In $B\otimes_AK$, the tensor relation gives $(b\otimes1)a^r=0$ [def-weil-module-base-change]. Since $a/1$ is invertible in the zero-prime localization $K$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], multiplication by $a^{-r}$ forces $b\otimes1=0$, a contradiction. Hence $C_a\ne0$ for every such $a$.

source.place: Tag 0575, lemma-nonreduced-in-neighbourhood, annihilator quotient and multiplication sequence; explicit fraction calculations

proof.text: Choose a finite polynomial presentation $P=A[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\twoheadrightarrow B$ using [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra, def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Through the resulting surjections $P\twoheadrightarrow C,D$, each of $C,D$ is a cyclic, hence finitely generated, $P$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. A domain is reduced: if $r^m=0$ with $m\geq1$, repeated use of the absence of zero divisors gives $r=0$. Apply [lem-sfb-reduced-polynomial-module-generic-freeness] separately with $R=A$, this finite $n$, and $M=C,D$. It gives dense opens $G_C,G_D\subset\operatorname{Spec}A$, each the union of principal opens on which the corresponding module is free. The spectrum is nonempty since $(0)$ is prime [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Thus each dense open is nonempty. Choose a point in $G_C$ and a principal open $D(u)$ in its defining union containing that point. Then $u$ is outside a prime, so $u\ne0$, and $C_u$ is free. In the same way choose $v\ne0$ with $D_v$ free. This uses no finite-presentation hypothesis on the quotient modules.

source.place: Tag 051Z, lemma-generic-flatness-reduced, polynomial-module case; used for the generic-freeness calls in Tag 0575

proof.text: Put $g=uv\ne0$. Inverting $g$ makes both $u$ and $v$ units, with $u^{-1}=v/g$ and $v^{-1}=u/g$. The fraction formulas identify $(A_u)_v=A_g$ and $(C_u)_v=C_g$: send $(x/u^i)/v^j$ to $x/(u^iv^j)$ and rewrite the denominator as a power of $g$; the inverse sends $x/g^k$ to $(x/u^k)/v^k$. Equality in both directions is precisely the fraction criterion [def-weil-ring-localization-away, def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away]. Take a basis $(e_i)$ of $C_u$ [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. Its images span $(C_u)_v$, by expanding the numerator of each fraction as a finite basis sum and dividing its coefficients by the denominator. For a finite relation among these images, clear their powers of $v$ in the coefficients. Vanishing in the localized module means some further power $v^k$ kills the resulting relation in $C_u$. Basis independence then says each resulting coefficient is killed by that power, so each original localized coefficient is zero. Thus these images are a basis of $C_g$ over $A_g$. Interchanging $u,v$ gives a basis of $D_g$ from the basis of $D_v$. This argument uses only finite support of individual expansions; either basis may be infinite or empty. Step 2 also gives $C_g\ne0$.

source.place: Tag 0575, lemma-nonreduced-in-neighbourhood, annihilator quotient and multiplication sequence; explicit fraction calculations

proof.text: The fraction formulas define $\iota_g((x+I)/g^n)=bx/g^n$ and $q_g(x/g^n)=(x+bB)/g^n$; these are $A_g$-linear and $q_g$ is surjective. If $bx/g^n=0$, some $g^kbx=0$, hence $g^kx\in I$ and $(x+I)/g^n=0$. Thus $\iota_g$ is injective. If $q_g(x/g^n)=0$, some $g^kx\in bB$; write $g^kx=by$. Then $x/g^n=by/g^{n+k}=\iota_g((y+I)/g^{n+k})$. Conversely $q_g\iota_g=0$ since every $by$ lies in $bB$. This proves exactness without invoking an uncited theorem about exactness of localization [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away, def-weil-ring-localization-away].

source.place: Tag 0575, lemma-nonreduced-in-neighbourhood, annihilator quotient and multiplication sequence; explicit fraction calculations

proof.text: The ring homomorphism $B_g\to C_g$, $x/g^n\mapsto(x+I)/g^n$, is surjective. Its kernel consists of fractions for which some $g^kx\in I$, equivalently $g^kbx=0$, equivalently $(b/1)(x/g^n)=0$. Thus its kernel is $\operatorname{Ann}_{B_g}(b/1)$. Sending a class of $x/g^n$ modulo this kernel to $(x+I)/g^n$ is a well-defined bijective ring homomorphism, giving the first canonical identification. Likewise the surjection $B_g\to D_g$ has kernel those $x/g^n$ with $g^kx=by$ for some $k,y$, exactly the elements $by/g^{n+k}$ of $(b/1)B_g$. Its quotient map gives the second canonical identification. All kernel equivalences are the defining fraction criterion [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away, def-weil-ring-localization-away]. Under the first identification the formula for $\iota_g$ in step 5 is multiplication by $b/1$, as required.
